title: Microsoft Teams: keypad consent for recording and transcription in one-to-one PSTN calls
summary: The briefing is supported by the roadmap, Microsoft's tenant notice and the cited documentation, including its warnings about conflicting documentation. The summary should explicitly say that the keypad prompt applies where explicit consent is required, rather than suggesting every PSTN call will receive it.

claims.claim: Teams will ask PSTN participants in one-to-one calls to press 1 or 2 before including them in recording or transcription.
claims.quote: PSTN participants in applicable one-to-one Teams calls where explicit consent for recording or transcription is required
claims.fix: Replace the summary with: "Where explicit consent is required, PSTN callers in one-to-one Teams calls will press 1 or 2 before recording or transcription includes them. No new setting; prepare users."

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe the one-to-one PSTN keypad prompt.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams PSTN one to one explicit consent keypad separate policy switch PowerShell ExplicitRecordingConsent; opened call-recording-transcription-captions and participant-agreement-recording-transcription. Keypad results cover Audio Conferencing, not this planned one-to-one change.

claims.claim: The call-recording Learn page describes a Yes or No consent prompt for call participants.
claims.quote: When a participant decides to un-mute, turn on their camera, or share content, they’re asked to respond 'Yes' or 'No' to consent to be included in the recording and transcription.

claims.claim: The calling-policy ExplicitRecordingConsent parameter covers both one-to-one VoIP and PSTN calls.
claims.quote: This parameter manages recording consent for Teams 1:1 VoIP and PSTN calls.

claims.claim: The meeting-consent Learn page currently lists PSTN endpoints in one-to-one calls as auto-consented.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Neither the roadmap record nor the supplied notice names a licence, meter or charge for the capability.
claims.quote: The capability uses the existing Teams calling policy for explicit recording consent rather than introducing a new policy setting.

claims.claim: The calling-policies Learn page describes this consent setting without naming a licence for it.
claims.quote: Require participant agreement for recording and transcription - When this is on, participants must agree to be recorded and transcribed.

claims.claim: The consent setting is at Teams admin center > Voice > Calling policies > policy > Edit > Require participant agreement for recording and transcription.
claims.quote: select Voice > Calling policies. ... Select the policy or policies that you want to modify, and then select Edit. ... Require participant agreement for recording and transcription

claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell documents Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExplicitRecordingConsent <string>, subject to the unreleased-feature caveat the briefing reports.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy ... [-Identity] <string> ... [-ExplicitRecordingConsent <string>] ... This setting controls whether users must provide or obtain explicit consent before recording a 1:1 PSTN or Teams call.

claims.where: controls[1]; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: No separate PSTN-only or keypad-only consent switch is documented in the UI or calling-policy PowerShell.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams PSTN one to one explicit consent keypad separate policy switch PowerShell ExplicitRecordingConsent. Opened teams-calling-policy and Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy; both document the shared setting. MC1530950 explicitly says no new admin policy setting is introduced.

claims.claim: The recording permission is at Teams admin center > Voice > Calling policies > policy > Cloud recording for calling.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Teams admin center, select Voice > Calling policies. ... Select the policy that you want to edit. ... Turn Cloud recording for calling to On.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity Global -AllowCloudRecordingForCalls $true enables recording in the global calling policy.
claims.quote: For example, this script enables call recording for the global policy: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity Global -AllowCloudRecordingForCalls $true

claims.claim: The transcription permission is at Teams admin center > Voice > Calling policies > policy > Transcription.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Teams admin center, select Voice > Calling policies. ... Select the policy you want to modify. ... Turn Transcription to On.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity Global -AllowTranscriptionForCalling $true enables transcription in the global calling policy.
claims.quote: For example, this script enables transcription for the global policy: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity Global -AllowTranscriptionForCalling $true

claims.claim: Audit searches are configured in Microsoft Purview portal > Audit > Search > Activities - friendly names.
claims.quote: Select the Audit solution card. ... On the Search page, configure the following search criteria as applicable: ... Activities - friendly names: Select the drop-down list to display the friendly names for audited activities that you can search for.
